analyzed_vuln.description: The HTML push-parser loop caches `avail = input->end - input->cur`, then invokes parsing/SAX work which can fatally stop the parser. `xmlHaltParser` frees the input buffer, sets `instate` to `XML_PARSER_EOF`, and replaces `cur/base/end` with the one-byte global empty-string literal. `htmlParseTryOrFinish` continues the current state case without rechecking EOF or recomputing `avail`, so later bounds decisions use the stale positive value and an indexed access such as `in->cur[1]` reads one byte past that global literal. The ASan line at 6095 is optimized/mismatched attribution within this state case; the root cause is stale input state and missing post-callback halt/bounds validation in `htmlParseTryOrFinish`, not the TSCII converter.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The fuzz harness derives options and an allocation limit from the first 8 bytes, then feeds the remainder through the HTML push parser in chunks. The document contains a `<meta charset=TSCII>` declaration followed by attacker-controlled high bytes (many `0x82` bytes and a final invalid/incomplete `0xff`). Processing the declared encoding/fatal error path causes `xmlStopParser`/`xmlHaltParser` while `htmlParseTryOrFinish` is already executing and still holds an `avail` value for the former buffer. Continued execution then accesses the replacement empty-string input using that stale availability, producing the global-buffer-overflow.

args: In libxml2/HTMLparser.c, analyze htmlParseTryOrFinish (definition starts around line 5498) for the safest minimal root-cause fix to stale `in`/`avail` after callbacks or parser helpers invoke xmlHaltParser. Is there an upstream patch pattern or a particularly suitable control-flow point? Identify all places within a switch iteration where execution can access `in->cur` after a SAX callback/helper could set `ctxt->instate = XML_PARSER_EOF` and replace the input buffer. Recommend whether a general post-switch check suffices or where immediate checks are required.

The supplied ASan reproducer enters the HTML push parser with `<meta charset=TSCII>` and malformed high bytes. `xmlHaltParser` in libxml2/parserInternals.c frees the input buffer, sets EOF, and sets base/cur/end to the global one-byte empty string. htmlParseTryOrFinish caches `in` and positive `avail` at loop entry. In the XML_PARSER_CONTENT text loop around lines 6084-6092, htmlParseCharData/htmlParseReference may halt, but line 6091 still reads `in->cur[0]`. Other state cases also call SAX callbacks and parsing helpers before accesses. I want a focused C-source fix under libxml2 that addresses changed input state/pointers, ideally consistent with upstream style, rather than only masking the exact PoC.
